traits.title: Headless SDK: ships no widget kit; its UI expectation is ui.cli (Node, Python)

Verified cache; construct and load offline

supports() and capability telemetry
features.note: Also proven by the parity gate: the capability table supports() reads is generated from the SDK's manifest into its constants module, and parity:check fails when the module's CAPABILITY_DIGEST is not the manifest's (P1b-10).

features.title: Secure token store, surfaced failure, no silent downgrade

allowedNa.why: A browser has no keyring; the session lives in an HttpOnly cookie.
The renderer holds no credentials; the host process's Node SDK keeps the token behind the bridge (packages/sdk-react/src/desktop/bridge.ts).

The OS keyring is reached through the optional @napi-rs/keyring addon, which cannot load inside a single-executable build or without a Secret Service; the token then lives in a 0600 file, Store.status() says keyring-unavailable and supports() says dependency (P1b-10).

The keyring backend is the optional `polaris-key[keyring]` extra; without it, or without a usable OS keyring, the token lives in a 0600 file, Store.status() says keyring-unavailable and supports() says dependency (P1b-10).

A JVM desktop process reaches no OS keyring (Keychain, Credential Manager, Secret Service) without a native library, which the Kotlin SDK does not ship; the token lives in a 0600 file, Store.status() says keyring-unavailable and supports() says dependency (P6-06). Android has the Keystore (P6-12).

features.title: Error, gate and activation copy: copy.message(code), copy.title(code)
features.note: The English base is conformance/parity/copy.en.json (copy.schema.json); gen:constants emits one generated copy module per SDK and refuses a key set that does not cover every errors.json code, every licenseStatus and every activationResult. The unit proof is each SDK's fallback and placeholder table (SDK-PARITY-PASS §3.2).

allowedNa.why: A browser has no hardware ids to anchor a keyless enrolment.
The renderer delegates enrolment to the host process's Node SDK, which holds the hardware ids.

features.title: Refusal link: manageUrl on device-limit, withManageReturn, withManageKey
features.note: PX-W8 (WIRE-CONTRACT-V4 §5.3): the result of a device-limit activation or enrolment exposes the Worker's manageUrl, validated (https, no userinfo, at most 2048 characters); the helpers add the app's return= and, on an /activate link, the fragment #key=. Never an auth failure. I-10a and I-10b extend this to key-entry-limit.

features.title: Entitlements, profile, licence id
features.note: The G11 rows are gate-matrix.json's entitlementRows family (isEntitled is isUsable(status) && value === true; a revoked licence with an enforced flag is not entitled). The corpus proof is attached by the last SDK G11 task to land (SP-N02, SP-R03, SP-P02, SP-S02, SP-K02, SP-G02; plans/SP-00.md D4).

features.title: entitledChannels()
features.note: PARITY §5.2 names cases.json, but no corpus case asserts entitledChannels yet (licenseDocCases only expect accept). Unit until a corpus case exists.

allowedNa.why: A browser session holds a cookie, not a registered device token, so there is no registration to repeat (follows devices.register on web).
The renderer holds no device token; the host process's Node SDK re-registers.

features.title: Typed activation results: every refusal by its body code, never a collapsed 403
features.note: Proven by activate-refusals.json (enroll_claimed, license_disabled, an expired licence's key, hardware_mismatch, rate_limited, each with today's server body: the Worker answers an expired licence with 401 unauthorized and a rate limit without Retry-After, and activation is not a trust operation, so attestation_required has no step; see packages/worker/test/transcripts/format.ts), recorded beside activate-enroll-deactivate.json so the SDKs that implement license.activate keep replaying that one unchanged (plans/SP-00.md D2; SDK-PARITY-PASS §3.1).

features.title: Precedence (enforced, default, local, environment)
features.note: The environment layer applies to desktop hosts only; in a browser it is empty by definition, which the matrix pins as each case's `expectNoEnv` answer rather than an N/A.

allowedNa.why: The Worker strips secrets from browser sessions.
The renderer never holds secrets; the host process's Node SDK resolves them (packages/sdk-react/src/desktop/desktopAdapter.ts).

features.title: Persisted device-local overrides: config.set, config.setting, onConfigChange
features.note: S-17 §5.11's names, so U-06 and U-20 add sync state under the same API. Device-local only. The unit proof persists, clears, validates against the catalog type and emits change events (SDK-PARITY-PASS §3.11).

allowedNa.why: A browser has no hardware ids; it uses a random id in IndexedDB.
The renderer cannot read hardware ids; the host process's Node SDK fingerprints the device.
A browser cannot read OS or hardware facts or probe for companion apps.
The renderer cannot read OS or hardware facts; the host process's Node SDK collects them.
Registration mints a bearer device token; the browser adapter is cookie-session based and holds none (packages/sdk-react/src/browser/browserAdapter.ts), and a browser has no hardware anchor.
The host process's Node SDK registers the device and holds its bearer; the renderer never sees it.

List, rename and deauthorise call /

/devices, which authenticates only with a device bearer token; a browser holds a cookie session and no bearer, so the browser adapter refuses with device-management-unsupported (packages/sdk-react/src/browser/browserAdapter.ts).

POST /

/devices/report accepts only a device bearer token; a browser holds a cookie session and no bearer, and cannot read the OS or hardware facts the report carries.

features.title: Update-health events: the journalled update events on devices/report

allowedNa.why:
The events ride POST /

/devices/report, which accepts only a device bearer token; a browser cookie session holds none (as devices.report; SP-R02's bearer mode removes both).

features.note: Proven by telemetry-report-updates.json: a 17-event journal drains as 16 then 1 (updatesPending 1, then 0), recorded beside telemetry-report.json rather than extending it (plans/SP-00.md D3; SDK-PARITY-PASS §3.13).

features.title: Device attestation (App Attest, Play Integrity) raising the trust level

allowedNa.why: A server or CLI process has no platform attestation service; only iOS App Attest and Android Play Integrity can raise a device to attested.
A CPython process has no platform attestation service.
A browser has no App Attest or Play Integrity; web devices stay at the basic trust level by design.
A desktop renderer has no platform attestation service.
App Attest is an iOS and iPadOS service; a desktop build stays basic.
Windows has no attestation service the Worker verifies; a desktop build stays basic.
Linux has no attestation service the Worker verifies; a desktop build stays basic.
A JVM desktop build has no attestation service the Worker verifies.
A .NET desktop build has no attestation service the Worker verifies.
A Tauri webview has no attestation service the Worker verifies.
Only a store install can attest: a sideloaded iOS build or an Android build not installed by Google Play cannot, and stays basic.
Device-code sign-in (RFC 8628) exists for inputs that cannot run a browser redirect; a browser is one, and signs in with the OIDC redirect (identity.oidc) instead.

features.title: Verify pkey-release+jws against pinned release keys
Verified download: bearer delivery, Range resume, size and SHA-256 checked
features.note: Proven by release-fetch-gated.json: a licensed-delivery fetch (200), a resumed one (Range/If-Range, 206) and, once the licence is disabled, the licensed mode's refusal (401 download_auth_required) (SDK-PARITY-PASS §3.6).

features.title: The distribution download model: platforms and the current build
features.note:
Proven by distribution-download-model.json (GET /

/distribution/download.json). It also owns the download page link, so no portal.links id exists (plans/SP-00.md D1; SDK-PARITY-PASS §3.8).

features.title: Native updater feed URLs: appcast, WinSparkle, Velopack, App Installer, zsync

allowedNa.why: A browser has no native updater to point at a feed; a web build updates through its service worker (update.driver).

features.note: Built from discovery's update.endpoints templates; a missing template is the typed unsupported (product). The proof is a generated corpus file rather than assertions in discovery-capabilities.json, which would stop that transcript applying where update.feeds is planned (plans/SP-00.md D5; SDK-PARITY-PASS §3.7).
